headline_marked: Meta launches enterprise AI platform, hires MongoDB CEO [[Chirantan Desai]]
headline: Meta launches enterprise AI platform, hires MongoDB CEO Chirantan Desai
summary: Meta is expanding its AI offerings to businesses with a new platform, led by the former CEO of MongoDB. The move aims to monetize Meta's significant AI investments.
details: Meta announced the launch of its "Meta Enterprise Platform" on Monday, a new initiative designed to extend the company's AI capabilities to corporate clients and businesses.

To spearhead this new venture, Meta has appointed Chirantan “CJ” Desai, the former CEO of database software company MongoDB. This move builds upon Meta's recent introduction of Muse, a personal AI assistant capable of tasks like sending emails and booking travel.

The platform will offer businesses access to Meta's comprehensive AI technology stack, including Muse, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, and Muse Code. Desai stated that AI will fundamentally redefine how organizations innovate and operate, and Meta aims to provide AI products and services for companies to deploy.

This strategic expansion into the enterprise AI market is expected to help Meta recoup its substantial investments in artificial intelligence. Concurrently, MongoDB's stock saw a significant drop of over 17% following the news of its CEO's immediate resignation, with Dev Ittycheria stepping in as interim chief executive.

topic: iphone duo gets first killer app with virtual walkman, new features rumored
headline_marked: [[iPhone Duo]] app mimics classic Walkman experience
headline: iPhone Duo app mimics classic Walkman experience
summary: An indie developer has created 'Duo-Man', an app that uses the foldable phone's dual screens to replicate the nostalgic feel of a cassette tape player.
details: Pre-orders for the new iPhone Duo begin in October, but the device may already have its first standout app. 'Duo-Man', developed by Vidit Bhargava, cleverly utilizes the Duo's unique dual-screen design to emulate the experience of using a classic Walkman.

The app takes advantage of the iPhone Duo's 7.6-inch inner foldable display and its 5.4-inch outer screen. Users can open the device to select their music and 'insert' a cassette tape, then close it to begin listening, mimicking the physical interaction of old cassette players.

Bhargava aimed for authenticity, incorporating recorded button clicks and static noise from a real Walkman into the app. He was inspired by the hinge mechanism of physical objects like the Walkman, seeing a parallel with foldable phones.

The app taps into the broader 'retro' tech trend, appealing to consumers drawn to classic physical devices. It also showcases the creativity often seen in the iOS developer community, leveraging Apple's robust App Store ecosystem.

Initially a hackathon project that won second place at the Bitrig hackathon, Duo-Man gained significant traction online, exceeding 1.8 million views. This positive reception has encouraged Bhargava to develop it into a full-fledged app.

Future updates are planned to include support for Apple Music and local files, with a unique feature allowing the use of Apple Pencil to 'roll' the cassette loop. Bhargava also intends to replicate the original Walkman's fast-forward and rewind functionality, with potential Spotify integration later.
